comments.value: Ooooh i love this! 100% actually recently upgradedy ram to 64GB but turn out my other friend was right after all, Vrchat Does have deep issues including memory leaks

details:
VRChat will crash after consuming every byte of RAM the system has available. RAM usage spikes occur with avatar load but do not 'trough' afterwards, indicating that at some point memory is not appropriately cleared.
Testing config:
Windows 10 Pro 21H2
Last Working VRC Version: 2022.2.1
Current Broken version: 2022.2.2
Systems Tested:
	System 1: 
		Ryzen 9 5950X
		128GB RAM
		GPU0: RTX 3090 Ti
		GPU1: RTX 3090 Ti
		Graphics Driver: Latest NVIDIA "Studio" Driver
		Remaining Drive Space: ~210GB
		Game installed to NVMe SSD
	
	System 2: 
		Ryzen 9 5950X
		64GB RAM
		GPU0: RTX 3090 Ti
		Graphics Driver: Latest NVIDIA "Studio" Driver
		Remaining Drive Space: ~20GB
		Game installed to NVMe SSD
	System 3:
		Ryzen 7 2700X
		32GB RAM
		GPU0: RTX 3080
		GPU1: RTX 3080
		Graphics Driver: Latest NVIDIA "Game Ready" Driver
		Remaining Drive Space: ~90GB
		Game installed to NVMe SSD
	VR Equipment tested with:
		Config 0: No VR Connected
		Config 1: HTC Vive Pro - 2 x Base Station 2.0 - Index Controllers
		Config 2: HTC Vive Cosmos - Vive Controllers
		
		
Steps to reproduce:
	- Start VRChat in VR mode using either the launcher from steam, or by running the exe directly
	- Enter a world that other users can access
	- Over time, RAM usage spikes to absurd levels (30GB in system 3, ~50GB in system 2, 100GB in system 1)
	- VRAM usage also climbs in short peaks, though not anywhere as severe
	- Once all RAM in the system is consumed, the process will hang
	- If the operating system watchdog notices the excessive consumption, the VRC window will render black. Audio will be present for ~ 5 seconds, then drop. VRC will then be force closed by the OS
	- If the operating system watchdog does not notice the RAM increase in time, the system will hang and require a power cycle
Observations:
	> RAM spikes proportional to avatar size can be observed when an avatar is loaded. When the avatar is unloaded, the RAM that the avatar appeared to consume sticks around.
	> This behaviour WAS present in prior versions, but required 5-6 hours of gameplay before issues occured. With 2022.2.2 this time has been dramatically 'improved' to less than half an hour!
	> In public worlds with multiple players arriving and leaving, this very quickly builds up RAM use. I suspect other users that don't have this problem simply do not have many friends.
	> RAM usage spikes get more severe the more avatars are loaded, which again, could just mean that a solution is to be less popular or do less stuff with fewer people.
	> In worlds with moderated avatar access (i.e. only green avatars), these spikes are SIGNIFICANTLY smaller
	> If VRChat is started in non-VR mode, the memory climb is reduced but not eliminated, but then, why the [expletive] are you playing this instead of secondlife.
	> Even with avatar safety settings set to the most strict, the peaks still exist, begging the question what the purpose of the safety settings actually is.
	> No excessive CPU use is observed, though putting up with this absolutely melts my brain if that counts.
	> Typical time to crash is about 15 to 30 minutes depending on number of users and how often they switch avatar, so good luck if any of your friends have ADHD.
	
Personal remarks:
	> Audit of the performance charecteristics at the server side does not appear to happen - the uploader's SDK client appears to be 'trusted' despite it being in an insecure domain. Subsequent game clients can be 'tricked' into downloading a file that has significantly worse performance charecteristics than is actually present
	> This, however, is not neccisary, as avatars are downloaded anyway even if they exceed the user's maximum avatar performance 
	> It would be a small architectural change to - at a minimum - have avatar performance metrics (even if from an untrusted source) downloaded prior to downloading the entire asset.
	
Attached is a google drive link to two logs from System 3. In 17-32-10 the process was suspended and VRChat was closed with SIGTERM. In 17-47-22, VRChat used every single byte of memory, caused the entire system to hang, and had to be ended with power-cycling.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DMRh_NvlSJJfFBn0-mYvFcMFS80xJwgJ?usp=sharing
Unprofessional remarks:
	Get your [expletive] sorted out. The game is now unplayable for me and becoming unplayable for many others with each update. I have spent over £8000 in VR equipment - including equipment for those that didn't have it, and many things that aren't used in VRChat because they're not supported - because I believe in the genre and the power it has to connect people. With VRChat's inability to make sensible buisiness decisions and it's pursuit of bizzare and proven ineffective monetisation strategies, I have zero confidence in putting any of my money with them. This is one of the big reasons why a lot of people including myself have never purchased VRC+ or ever plan on giving y'all a penny unless you actually show it's not going to be supporting an unsupportable model.
	
	Developers with a passion are great but if they can't develop reliably then you're [expletive]'d. Instead of punching down on mod developers, use that 80 million dollars of investment you got a few months back and give them incentives to join your staff. Instead of pursuing bizzare forms of monetisation that are unsustainable, pursue the ones your investors actually invested in you to see - do like secondlife and make an integrated asset marketplace with fiat, or like Minecraft and monetise your mod scene. 
	
	VRChat was how I was able to stay in contact with my girlfriend on the other side of the planet during COVID. If you really want to embrace the publicity that you get from documentaries that talk about this sort of thing, then stop [expletive]ing [expletive]ing on the [expletive]ing [expletive] that made it happen, make a decent [expletive]ing decision for once, and fix your [expletive] when you do [expletive] it up.
Do Better,
Mod
